steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease an 8x8-inch baking dish.
Spread chopped plums evenly into the prepared baking dish and sprinkle with 1/4 cup sugar.
Mix flour, remaining 3/4 cup sugar, baking powder, and salt together in a large bowl; stir in beaten egg. Spoon mixture over plums and drizzle batter with melted butter.
Bake in the preheated oven until fruit is bubbling and topping is golden brown and crisp, about 40 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Plum Crisp
raw_recipe.description: This plum crisp is a simple fruit dessert with a sweet and crispy baked buttery topping that uses fresh summer plums for an easy, delicious treat.
raw_recipe.name: Plum Crisp

review.reviewBody: Perfect recipe for all those plums you don't know what to do with. I added two eggs because mine were small and sprinkled my plums with cinnamon and vanilla before adding the batter. After putting the batter on top I sprinkled just a little brown sugar on the top. Thanks for a wonderful recipe!

I had several plums and a couple nectarines left over and thank for this recipe. I am gluten free and so I had to change it a little bit. I used Bob's Red Mill gluten free 1 to 1 baking flour. I added the melted butter to the dry ingredients. I then put the topping over the fruit. I had to cook it 20 min longer and it turned out like a cobbler. I was delightful. I have never used plums in a cobbler but after making this I will now. Thank you.

I read some of the reviews and followed their tweaks. I used 2 beaten eggs as my plums were small. added1/2tsp vanilla and 1/2 tsp cinnamon to plum mixture. followed rest per recipe. Sprinkled a bit of sugar on top and a sprinkle of cinnamon before baking. This was amazing! Perfect mix of sweet and tangy. I will be making this a lot, and my guests at the table agreed it was a keeper, and asked for the recipe. Mine didn't get too crispy, but was super delicious. there were no leftovers. thank you for sharing this recipe.

It is not really the season for plums but I saw some in the store and had to try this! I used 6 very large plums ((between 5 and 6 cups) and let them ripen in fruit basket 5 days before using. I was afraid they weren’t as sweet as I would have liked, so I tossed them with 1/3 cup sugar. 1 tsp of vanilla and sprinkled with cinnamon as other viewers suggested. My crisp needed 45 minutes in the oven. So good and not too sweet!

Great recipe. I used half flour and half rolled oats. I used brown sugar with the flour mixture and probably used 3/4 c (I didn't measure). I also didn't melt the butter and I just used soften butter and crumbled/mixed it with the flour with my hands. Cooked in toaster oven at 350 for 30 minutes and it was perfect.

I doubled the recipe. I used about 16 black plums. They were quite sweet, so I skipped adding sugar to the plums. I added about a teaspoon of allspice to the flour and sugar and two teaspoons of vanilla to the eggs of my double batch. I did not double the butter, instead used only the original 1/2 cup. We all loved it and will gladly make again. Thank you for a wonderful recipe!

I added a little cinnamon and vanilla to the fruit blend. I didn't have any plums so I used fresh fruit: peaches (2), nectarines (2), small apricots (3) and then some frozen berries to equal recipe fruit amount.

Out of this world! I used 16 plums from my tree with only half cup almond flour. I used 1/4 cup honey instead of sugar on the plums & reduced the other brown (I used) sugar by 1/4 cup. I also used vegan “egg-replacer” by Red Mill to make a bit healthier and only used 1/4 cup melted butter. Absolutely delicious and a great way to use up plums that fall to the ground (easily cutting out bad parts).

I love how easy this recipe is to assemble. Easy ingredients. I also had apples and peaches. So I added those in with increasing a little more dry topping but keeping the same amount of butter drizzle, the cobbler came out beautifully! I did add 3 minutes to the bake time for extra crispy! This will likely be our go to Summer dessert with vanilla ice cream!!

This is super yummy!! My Husband said it was his new favorite dessert. Those are the words I strive to hear!! 😄 I doubled recipe, used a little less salt, and added the melted butter right to the batter which made a lovely finish!!

Big hit with our family! I added vanilla and cinnamon to the chopped plums as others mentioned. I switched up 1/2 the granulated sugar in the topping for brown sugar. I swapped 1/2 the flour for quick-cooking oats. I also added about 1/4 cup of roughly chopped pecans to the topping for a little texture. This was a great recipe to make use of the plums I had on hand! I will definitely make again when I have peaches or plums around.
Took this dessert to a party and it was a hit!!!! No left overs... lol
Nice!

I did the same as rotorwife (added a tish of cinnamon and a teeny bit of brown sugar). Easy to make, baked up beautifully. Taking to a party but looks delicious (wish I could taste it right now! PS - I had 10 plums, so I also added a few rehydrated dried tart cherries (about a handful across the top) before adding topping. Looks spectacular! Thanks for the recipe. Pic is as it was going into the oven. Review after party with finished product pic to follow.
It nade more of a dough than a batter. Missing a liquid maybe. I cut the dough into chunks and placed on top of the plum sugar mixture. Will see how it turns out.
Add cinnamon and red sugar topping.

Thank you for sharing this recipe. :) What an easy and great-tasting recipe!! I added 2 eggs as the dough was very dry. I also added a teaspoon of vanilla essence to the dough and orange zest to the plums. So yummy!!
I added an extra egg, but forgot to drizzle the melted butter on, so it turned out more like a cobbler. It was delicious.

Fantastic recipe. Only changes for me were I added 2 more plums for a total of 14 and one extra egg even though I had large eggs. Gave the dough more umph. Thank you for this super easy dessert recipe.

Delicious! I doubled the amount of prune plums because I had so many and glad I did. Otherwise wouldn’t have been enough fruit. I used 1/2 cup brown sugar and 1/4 cup white sugar in the topping for extra flavor. Next time I’ll use less sugar with the plums as it was to sweet.
